text:
marina: Heads up — after the OFED + kernel pack rolled to eu-west2 GPU pool we're seeing a ~40-60% regression in NCCL allreduce bandwidth for large batch jobs. Noticed at 05:20 UTC. :warning:

ajay: Which job/cluster? can you paste the perf numbers?

marina: p3x-large like farm (32-GPU). Quick perf snapshot from the run before vs after:
```
before: NCCL allreduce 48 GB/s aggregate
after : NCCL allreduce 22-30 GB/s aggregatesamples: 4096 seq_len 2048
```

marina: dmesg on one of the hosts shows repeated mlx5 warnings and CQ messages:
```
[  123.456789] mlx5_core 0000:01:00.0: EQ overflow
[  123.457012] mlx5_core 0000:01:00.0: CQ overrun, cq cqn=0x2a
[  123.457345] mlx5_core 0000:01:00.0: mlx5_core: ERR event: PORT 1 link down
```

marina: `ethtool -S mlx5_core` also shows a spike in "tx_cq_overflow" and "rx_cq_overflow" counters after the rollout.

ryan: Deploy-bot shows OFED version bumped to 5.7.1 and kernel to 6.1.15 on the pool earlier this morning.

deploy-bot: deploy job `ofed-upgrade-eu-west2-2026-03-18` finished: success.

ajay: Could be CQ trimming heuristics in newer FW/driver interacting badly with NCCL's ring/bcast paths. Are we seeing bigger packet sizes or more small RDMA messages?

marina: Packet sizes look normal; but we do see more burstiness — NCCL switching to fewer, larger eager fragments due to a change in CUDA/kernel scheduling. Hard to prove.

sre_olga: Can we confirm fallback to RC->UD or IP fallback? `ibv_devinfo` and `nvidia-smi topo -m` look fine. I ran `nvidia-bench nccl --reduce` and it shows stall windows that align with the EQ overflows.

marina: I uploaded a host-level capture to the infra bucket: gs://redwood-infra/efa/1958880123/capture.tar.gz (contains ethtool, dmesg, ib_devinfo, perf).

ajay: Quick mitigation options:
- rollback OFED to previous package (5.5.x) on eu-west2 GPU pool (fast, known-good)
- apply mlx5 firmware microcode rollback (requires host reboot, slower)
- force NCCL to different transport (NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME / NCCL_IB_DISABLE) for canary jobs

ryan: For canary I'd try `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` on one job to confirm it's RDMA-related (will fall back to socket/tcp). If bandwidth recovers, we have a smoking gun.

marina: Ran that: with `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` same job hits ~46 GB/s again. So RDMA path is definitely impacted.

sre_olga: Okay -- plan: 1) Pause further OFED rollouts, 2) schedule rollback on remaining hosts in the pool, 3) patch release notes + incident ticket. Who can run the rollback job?

ryan: I'll own the rollback for eu-west2. Rolling batch of 20 hosts at a time, test nccl perf after each batch.

ajay: Add a quick health-check in infra-ci to run `nvidia-bench nccl --reduce` post-upgrade going forward. Also add guard: if NCCL aggregate drops >15% trigger rollback.

marina: Thanks. I'll open the incident and attach the perf captures. tagging @oncall to monitor production jobs. :white_check_mark:

infra-ci: CI job `nccl-smoke-eu-west2` queued as part of rollback verification.

marina: notes: we should also talk to vendor about EQ/CQ handling in 5.7.x OFED + mlx5 fw combo. might be a regression in event coalescing or CQ trimming under bursty workloads.

ryan: Rolling back first batch now, will post updates here every 15m.

marina: ETA for first 20 hosts rollback + verification ~40m.

ajay: Good catch, and good call on the `NCCL_IB_DISABLE` test — that made this triage quick.

marina: keeping this thread for rollback updates.
